=== Morphological Assessment Form ===
A. Leaf Arrangement & Architecture
    1. Leaf relative position (alternate / opposite / whorled): whorled (multiple leaves radiate from a single central node, visible in top-down views)
    2. Leaf spacing (clustered / distal): clustered (leaves are grouped closely at the terminal end of the shoot)
B. Leaf Complexity
    3.	Leaf complexity (simple / compound): simple (each leaf is a single blade without leaflets)
    4.	Compound leaf type, ONLY if leaf complexity is compound (odd-pinnate / even-pinnate): N/A
    5.	Number of leaflets (integer estimate 2, 4, 8, …): N/A
    6.	Leaflet arrangement (opposite / alternate / subopposite): N/A
C. Leaf Morphology
    7.	Leaf margin (entire / toothed) AND if toothed (dentate, serrate, etc.)): entire (leaf edges are smooth and continuous)
    8.	Leaf shape (elliptic, obovate, lanceolate, etc.): lanceolate (leaf is longer than wide, tapering to a point at both ends)
    9.	Leaf apex (acute, obtuse, acuminate): acute (leaf tip tapers to a distinct, sharp point)
    10.	Leaf base (rounded, cordate, cuneate): rounded (leaf base is broadly curved)
    11.	Venation type (pinnate / palmate / parallel): pinnate (single midrib with secondary veins branching off)
    12.	Secondary veins (visibility, spacing, number): visible, closely spaced, and parallel to each other
    13.	Leaf surface features (glabrous, shiny, dull, rugose): dull (leaf surface lacks strong reflection or gloss)
    14.	Leaf surface trichomes (present / absent): absent (leaf surface appears smooth without visible hairs)
    15.	Petiole length (short / long): short (petioles are very short, appearing sessile or subsessile)
    16.	Petiole features (winged / grooved / terete): terete (petioles appear round in cross-section)
D. Stem & Shoot Traits
    17.	Stem type, may not be visible (woody / herbaceous): herbaceous (stem appears green, thin, and flexible rather than thick and brown)
    18.	Stem trichomes (present / absent): absent (stem surface appears smooth)
    19.	Stem color: green
    20.	Stem texture (smooth / ridged / lenticellate): smooth
E. Other Visible Seedling Traits
    21.	Stipules, sometimes visible only in close-up images (present / absent): absent (no stipules visible at leaf bases)
    22.	Latex, rarely visible but extremely diagnostic when present (present / not observed): not observed
    23.	Pulvinus, for Fabaceae family only (present / absent): absent (no swollen joint visible at leaf base)
    24.	Tendrils (present / absent): absent
F. Notes: A small pink flower bud is visible in the center of the leaf whorl. Some minor surface blemishes and holes are present on the leaves.
